spec: docs/spec/midgard-tx.md §8.10 — Cost claims: the carriage exit measurements
note:
Every execution figure §8.10 publishes is a row or a derivation here. Regenerate with `node scripts/verify-carriage-exec-ledger-v1.mjs --update`, and move the spec in the same commit.

**#592 re-take, one fixed per-view amount.** The six `tier3_corner_*` rows that open the door rose by exactly +5,944 mem / +1,838,206 cpu; `tier3_corner_fixture_only`, which opens none, did not move, and neither did any certificate-handler row. #592 needs tier 3 read two ways — lazily, which is `certified_view` and is what these rows measure, and materialised whole, which is `authenticated_whole_field_view`, because the validation machine's phases consume §5.2's item count and the lazy view refuses to answer it for a variable-width field. Both ways need the identical §8.4/§8.6 manifest checks, so those moved into one `certified_chunks` returning a `CertifiedChunksV1` record, and a tier-3 view construction pays one record construction and destructure more.

**#592 round-4 re-take, §8.3 erratum E1's repair of `K` (15,900 → 15,148).** `K` is the split, so this moves the fixture's chunk shape and therefore every row that hashes a chunk: the corner now splits `[15,148, 15,148, 2,467]` instead of `[15,900, 15,900, 963]`, and the two straddling reads are items 378 and 757 instead of 397 and 794. Two baselines are in play, because the re-take above is uncommitted as well, and every figure below names which one it is on: **cumulative** is against the last committed rows and so carries both re-takes; **round-4-only** is this re-take alone, i.e. the cumulative figure less the +5,944 mem / +1,838,206 cpu the paragraph above records for a door row. Direction and cause, row by row. `tier3_corner_fixture_only` is unmoved on either basis — it never opens the door and the fixture bytes are the same 32,763. Every door row gains a small fixed memory amount, because `expected_chunk_count` and the per-read `offset / chunk_bytes_k` arithmetic run against a smaller divisor over a three-chunk manifest: cumulatively **+8,268 on the open and +8,168 on each of the five read rows**, which is **round-4-only +2,324 on the open and +2,224 on each read row**. The open pays 100 mem more than a read does, which is why the derived per-read memory falls by 100 (155,242 → 155,142) while the derived open cost rises by the whole +8,268. CPU moves the other way on the reads — a full chunk is 752 bytes shorter, so each `blake2b_256` over the chunk a read lands in is cheaper: round-4-only −1,673,873 on the first read, −4,030,547 on the two-read row, and −2,459,431 and −102,757 on the two straddling reads (the cumulative figures for those four rows are +164,333, −2,192,341, −621,225 and +1,735,449, which read as increases or as shallower falls only because the earlier re-take's +1,838,206 is still inside them). The open is dearer on CPU on both bases: cumulative +2,537,007, round-4-only +698,801. The ragged-tail read gets **dearer** on CPU too — round-4-only **+5,396,149**, cumulative +7,234,355 — because that chunk grew from 963 to 2,467 bytes. The certificate-handler rows were not moved by the earlier re-take, so for them the two bases coincide: all six fall on CPU (−1,570,928 to −5,531,336) for the same chunk-length reason, and two of them fall on memory as well — `certificate_mint_cost_at_the_smallest_tier3` by −188 and `certificate_mint_cost_at_the_corner` by −282 — so the two mint derived deltas fall on both axes rather than on CPU alone.

**One conclusion moved with it, and it is not a rounding change: the read budget's binding axis is now memory, not CPU.** At the superseded `K` the corner admitted 83.5 reads by memory and 82.2 by CPU; at the repaired `K` it admits 83.5 by memory and 84.3 by CPU, because the per-read CPU fell and the per-read memory did not. The budget itself is essentially unchanged (≈82 → ≈83 items) — what changed is which axis is quoted as binding, and §8.10 says so rather than letting the number drift under an unchanged sentence.

**#606 re-take, 2026-08-16 — the E2 certificate repair (and, on the door rows only, `3eb41df7`).** All thirteen rows moved and four of the eight derived figures with them; this paragraph is the cause note the re-take owed. Bisected against pristine `git archive` builds of the intervening commits rather than assumed: the pexcludes rider `139a8ca3` leaves every row below identical to the batch base `854fea09` to the unit, so the whole of the movement is the E2 repair commit `d528e00b` — constant certificate asset name, mint-welded `field_hash`, the door's new equality of that `field_hash` against the commitment derived from the anchored structures, and the deletion of `carriage_reaches_the_anchor`. One later commit adds a second, separable amount, named in (3) below.

(1) **The six `tier3_corner_*` door rows each fall by 4,555 mem and rise by 32,936,197 cpu**, identically — the row that opens the door and the five that read through it alike. `tier3_corner_fixture_only`, which opens no door, moves differently again (−4,280 mem / +32,560,096 cpu), so the fixture and the door both moved and neither figure is the other's. That the six door rows move by one shared amount is what the five per-read derived subtractions prove: each is a difference of two rows that moved identically, so **all five are unchanged to the unit**, and with them the `readBudget` block and #592's conclusion that the read budget's binding axis is memory. Only `opening the three-chunk corner` moved among the read-side derivations, to 238,938 mem / 72,165,615 cpu, because it alone subtracts the fixture-only row from a door row.

(2) **All six certificate-handler rows fall on both axes**, by much more than the door rows move: `certificate_mint_fixture_only_smallest_tier3` −260,125 mem / −119,977,728 cpu, `certificate_mint_cost_at_the_smallest_tier3` −263,186 / −120,886,811, `certificate_mint_fixture_only_at_the_corner` −181,160 / −79,041,094, `certificate_mint_cost_at_the_corner` −182,220 / −79,577,844, `certificate_spend_fixture_only` −261,425 / −120,185,728, `certificate_spend_cost` −269,757 / −107,402,879. The three derived handler figures fall with them (mint at K+1 to 639,866 mem / 261,084,135 cpu, mint at the corner to 737,881 / 357,434,675, spend to 228,343 / 125,721,866). The fixtures fell as far as the handlers did, which is the shape to read carefully: most of what moved here is what a *test* must build to present a certificate, not what the handler charges to check one. **Which of the repair's four changes carries how much of the fall is NOT settled by these readings and is not published as one** — the candidates are the retired `blake2b_256(field_index_byte ‖ tx_id)` asset-name derivation (now a literal at every token reference), the datum's new `field_hash` field, the mint's new weld `expect`, and the door's new equality, and nothing measured here separates them.

(3) **A further +200 mem / +32,000 cpu on the six door rows**, and on nothing else, charged by `3eb41df7` (the §8.6 certificate field-index bound routed through `field_count`). Measured at `2a64d6f9` → `3eb41df7`, where `tier3_corner_fixture_only` is unmoved to the unit, so it is paid once per door opening that decodes a certificate datum. The same +200 / +32,000 appears on the tier-3 byte-bound rows of `canonical-decodability-exec-ledger-v1.json` and `committed-field-shape-exec-ledger-v1.json`. This amount landed **after** the batch's first ledger re-take (`7158377e`) and left this ledger red until the present one — recorded rather than absorbed, because a ledger that is red between two commits of the same batch is exactly what these verifiers exist to say out loud.

No judgement in this ledger moves: no `basisFit`, no `readBudget` figure, and the memory-binding conclusion above stands at the new numbers. The spec rows §8.10 pins move in the docs commit of this batch.
